concepts.title: The Idea and Evolution of Democracy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Idea and Evolution of Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: Democracy - rule by the people - has evolved over time from ancient assemblies and limited franchises to the modern universal adult franchise, shaping today's understanding that every adult citizen has an equal voice in choosing the government.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Idea and Evolution of Democracy'.
questions.a: Rule of the people has widened step by step: from few voices to universal franchise.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Features of Democratic Government' refers to.
questions.a: Democracy works through defining features: rulers are elected by the people, power is limited by a constitution, fundamental rights protect citizens, independent courts review actions, and governments remain accountable through discussion, debate and periodic elections.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Features of Democratic Government'.
questions.a: Election, constitution, rights and accountability - the four pillars that keep democracy standing.

concepts.title: Democracy in India: Strengths and Challenges

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Democracy in India: Strengths and Challenges' refers to.
questions.a: India adopted democracy with universal franchise in 1950, an extraordinary step for a diverse and newly free society; its strengths include regular elections and constitutional rights, while challenges such as inequality, social discrimination and money power test the system's health.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Democracy in India: Strengths and Challenges'.
questions.a: Democracy is a journey, not a destination: Indian democracy keeps defending and deepening itself.
